definition: A shafted mountaineering tool with a pick and spike used for support, balance, anchoring, and fall-arrest functions depending on design and terrain.
primary_role: Support and traction on snow or ice; emergency fall arrest; technical climbing
compatibility_or_notes: Classic, technical, and glacier-travel axes serve different terrain and movement demands.
safety_note: Select an axe appropriate to the intended activity and learn its use before entering technical terrain.

definition: Spiked attachments fitted to compatible boots to provide traction on snow and ice.
primary_role: Traction on hard snow and ice
typical_context: Glaciers; snow slopes; ice; mixed terrain
compatibility_or_notes: Must fit the boot and suit the intended activity; designs range from classic to technical.
safety_note: Poor fit or incompatible boots can compromise security.

definition: Protective mountain footwear designed to provide support, insulation, and a suitable interface with crampons.
compatibility_or_notes: Boot stiffness and crampon compatibility must match the intended terrain.
safety_note: Crampons should be fitted to compatible footwear and checked before use.

definition: Protective headgear designed to reduce injury risk from impacts and falling objects.
typical_context: Rock; ice; mixed terrain; high mountain routes
compatibility_or_notes: Should be appropriate for climbing and mountaineering use.
safety_note: A helmet does not eliminate hazards from rockfall, icefall, or falls.

definition: Wearable load-bearing equipment that connects a climber to ropes, protection, and related systems.
compatibility_or_notes: Different designs prioritize low weight, gear carrying, or adjustability.
safety_note: Use a harness intended for the activity and inspect it before use.

definition: A rope designed for climbing systems and fall protection, with properties determined by its construction and rating.
primary_role: Belaying, protection, rappelling, and team connection
compatibility_or_notes: Rope type and diameter must match the intended system and device.
safety_note: Use ropes within their rated applications and inspect for damage.

definition: A dynamic rope intended to be used as part of a two-rope system, with both ropes managed according to the applicable technique.
primary_role: Protection and rope management on routes requiring a double-rope system
compatibility_or_notes: Must be used as a half-rope system and with compatible hardware.
safety_note: Do not treat half ropes as interchangeable with single-rope systems.

definition: A lightweight dynamic rope designed to be used as a matched pair in a twin-rope system.
primary_role: Lightweight protection and descent systems on suitable routes
compatibility_or_notes: Both ropes are clipped together according to the rope system's requirements.
safety_note: Use only in configurations permitted by the rope's certification and manufacturer.

definition: A rope intended to provide additional security during mountain walking, glacier travel, or ski mountaineering.
primary_role: Team security on relatively straightforward terrain
compatibility_or_notes: Different from a full climbing rope in intended use.
safety_note: Use according to manufacturer and activity-specific guidance.

definition: A connector with a locking gate used to reduce the chance of accidental opening in appropriate climbing systems.
primary_role: Connecting ropes, devices, anchors, and harnesses
compatibility_or_notes: Shape and gate type should suit the connected device or system.
safety_note: Confirm that the gate and locking mechanism are correctly engaged before loading.

definition: A length of webbing formed into a loop and used for anchors, extensions, and equipment connections.
compatibility_or_notes: Lengths and materials vary by application.
safety_note: Use only certified slings in appropriate configurations and inspect for damage.

definition: A friction device used to control a climbing rope during belaying and, for suitable devices, rappelling.
primary_role: Rope control during climbing and descent
compatibility_or_notes: Device type must match rope type and diameter.
safety_note: Compatibility between device and rope is essential.

definition: A rope-grabbing device designed to allow controlled progress along a compatible rope, commonly on fixed lines.
primary_role: Ascent of fixed ropes and some rescue systems
compatibility_or_notes: Requires a compatible rope and appropriate attachment system.
safety_note: Use only within the manufacturer's intended configuration.

definition: Accessory cord used to form friction hitches such as a Prusik.
compatibility_or_notes: Cord diameter and rope compatibility affect friction-hitch behavior.
safety_note: Requires practical training to configure and load correctly.

definition: A tubular screw-in protection device designed for suitable ice and used as protection or an anchor component.
compatibility_or_notes: Effectiveness depends on ice quality, placement, and loading direction.
safety_note: Requires training in evaluating ice and placing protection.

definition: An anchor device or system designed to transfer load into suitable snow.
primary_role: Anchoring ropes or rescue systems in snow
compatibility_or_notes: Anchor type and effectiveness depend on snow structure and loading.
safety_note: Snow anchors require appropriate assessment and construction.

definition: A tool used to assist in creating an ice V-thread anchor for suitable descent or anchor systems.
compatibility_or_notes: Used with suitable ice conditions and compatible cord or rope systems.
safety_note: Requires hands-on training in ice-anchor construction.

definition: A pulley used to redirect rope or provide mechanical advantage in hauling systems.
compatibility_or_notes: Pulley selection depends on rope diameter, load, and intended system.
safety_note: Rescue hauling systems require training and appropriate anchors.

definition: A collection of rope, pulley, friction-hitch, anchor, and connection equipment assembled for crevasse rescue.
primary_role: Self-rescue and partner rescue from crevasses
compatibility_or_notes: Exact contents vary by team and route.
safety_note: A kit is only useful when the team knows how to use it.

definition: A hands-free light source used for movement, navigation, and camp tasks in darkness.
typical_context: Early starts; late descents; camps; emergencies
compatibility_or_notes: Carry spare or backup power for remote expeditions.
safety_note: Lighting is critical for route finding and emergency management in darkness.

definition: A waterproof and wind-resistant outer layer intended to protect against precipitation and wind.
typical_context: High mountain routes; snow; rain; wind
compatibility_or_notes: Material and design vary by intended activity.
safety_note: A shell is an outer protective layer, not a substitute for insulation.

definition: An insulated outer garment designed to reduce heat loss in cold environments.
primary_role: Thermal protection during cold periods and stops
typical_context: High camps; summit pushes; cold alpine environments
compatibility_or_notes: Insulation may be down or synthetic; performance depends on conditions and moisture.
safety_note: Keep insulation dry and select insulation appropriate to the environment.

definition: Protective coverings worn over boots and lower legs to reduce snow, water, and debris entry.
typical_context: Snow; glaciers; wet or loose terrain
compatibility_or_notes: Must fit the boot and activity.
safety_note: Do not treat gaiters as a substitute for suitable boots or crampon compatibility.

definition: A terrain representation used for route planning and navigation.
compatibility_or_notes: Best used with compass, altimeter, and other navigation information.
safety_note: Maps can become unreliable when terrain or route conditions change; verify current information.

definition: A magnetic navigation instrument used to determine direction and support map-based navigation.
compatibility_or_notes: Used together with a map and appropriate navigation method.
safety_note: Requires training in map-and-compass navigation.

definition: An instrument that estimates elevation, usually from atmospheric pressure.
compatibility_or_notes: Readings can change with weather and pressure.
safety_note: Use as an aid to navigation rather than as the sole source of position information.

definition: A satellite-based positioning system used to determine location and support navigation.
compatibility_or_notes: Works best with appropriate power management and map data.
safety_note: Electronic navigation should have a backup plan.

definition: A system that supplies additional oxygen to a climber at high altitude.
primary_role: Supplemental oxygen during selected high-altitude expeditions
compatibility_or_notes: System normally includes cylinder, regulator, mask, and associated components.
safety_note: Use is expedition-specific and requires appropriate training and medical/technical planning.

definition: A mask used as part of a supplemental oxygen system to deliver oxygen to the user.
compatibility_or_notes: Must match the oxygen system and regulator.
safety_note: Incorrect fit or system use can compromise oxygen delivery.

definition: An insulated sleeping system designed for very cold mountain environments.
primary_role: Thermal protection during high-altitude camps and bivouacs
compatibility_or_notes: Temperature performance depends on insulation, moisture, and user conditions.
safety_note: Choose insulation appropriate to the expected environment and keep it dry.
